objectives.statement: Distinguish authentication, which establishes a user's identity, from authorization, which determines access to resources.
objectives.citation: Overview of ASP.NET Core Authentication; Introduction to authorization in ASP.NET Core

objectives.statement: Identify ClaimsPrincipal and its identities and claims as the representation of the authenticated subject available to authorization checks.
Explain an ASP.NET Core authentication scheme as the named configuration that selects an authentication handler and its behavior.
Identify the Authorize attribute as a way to require an authenticated or otherwise authorized user for a controller, action, page or resource.
objectives.citation: Introduction to authorization in ASP.NET Core

objectives.statement: Relate UseAuthentication and UseAuthorization middleware to the request pipeline, with authentication establishing the user before authorization evaluates access.
Explain a claim as a name-value pair describing what a subject is rather than directly describing what the subject can do.
Explain a claim-based policy that requires the presence of a claim and apply it through an Authorize policy name.
Identify policies, requirements and handlers as the extensible pieces used to express and evaluate authorization rules.
Explain role-based authorization as requiring a user to belong to one or more named roles, commonly through Authorize Roles.
Distinguish comma-separated roles in one Authorize attribute as alternative roles where membership in any listed role can satisfy the role condition.
Explain that applying multiple Authorize role attributes requires membership in all of the roles specified by those attributes.
Relate role requirements expressed in an authorization policy to RequireRole during policy registration.
Identify MVC filters as components that run before or after particular stages of the MVC action pipeline.
Explain authorization filters as the filters that run first in the MVC filter pipeline and can short-circuit the request when authorization fails.
Distinguish resource, authorization, action, exception and result filters by the stage or concern of the MVC pipeline they address.
Explain that filters can be registered globally or applied to a controller or action, with scope affecting where they run in the pipeline.
Identify AllowAnonymous as an exception that bypasses authorization checks for an action or endpoint otherwise covered by authorization metadata.
objectives.citation: Introduction to authorization in ASP.NET Core

objectives.statement: Distinguish an authentication challenge for an unauthenticated request from a forbid result for an authenticated request that lacks permission.
objectives.citation: Introduction to authorization in ASP.NET Core

objectives.statement: Diagnose authorization middleware placed before authentication as an invalid pipeline arrangement because authorization needs the established user context.
Apply policy-based authorization when access depends on claims or requirements that are more precise than a simple role membership check.
